memos.headline: S08 and S07 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S01 and S02 Are Broken — Positioning Accordingly
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of December 5. S07 is sitting at its 52-week high with +39.8% over 12 weeks, RSI at 70, and massive relative strength vs SPY (+35.6% over 12w) — a textbook momentum leader, though the stretched extension (+45.8% above the 200d) warrants tight risk management. S08 is the cleanest trend: +21.2% over 12w, only -2.6% from highs, RSI a comfortable 59.4, and +16.9% relative strength over 12w — I have the most conviction here. On the other side, S01 is in a confirmed downtrend: -9.5% below its 200d mean, RSI 36.7, -18.6% drawdown, and -13.8% relative strength over 12w. S02's -45.8% drawdown from its 52-week high and -8.6% below the 200d mean signal severe structural damage despite a recent 4-week bounce. S05 is the wildcard — parabolic +90.1% over 26w and RSI 70.1 at just -0.7% from highs, but +17% above the 50d and +56% above the 200d screams overextension and mean-reversion risk.

views.note: Strongest risk-adjusted trend in the universe: near highs, healthy RSI 59, +16.9% 12w relative strength; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~265).
At 52w high with dominant momentum (+39.8% 12w, +35.6% rel strength), but +45.8% above 200d and RSI 70 raise pullback risk; a close below 570 would change my view.
Parabolic move (+90% 26w) with RSI 70.1 and +17% above 50d is unsustainable near-term; respecting the trend but not chasing — would get long on a pullback to the 50d (~275).
Orderly uptrend near highs (-1.7% drawdown) but flat relative strength vs SPY over 4w and 12w offers no edge; needs a breakout above 320 to get interested.
Quiet, low-vol name with RSI 51 and negligible relative strength; no catalyst in the chart to take a directional view.
Persistent downtrend: RSI 36.7, -9.5% below 200d, -13.8% 12w relative strength; would reconsider only on a reclaim above the 200d mean (~158).
Massive -45.8% drawdown from 52w high and trading -8.6% below 200d mean signals structural damage; recent bounce is noise until price reclaims the 200d (~362).
Below 50d mean by 4.8%, RSI 42, and -7.8% 12w relative strength indicate distribution; needs to hold 470 or risk accelerating lower.
Weakening 4w return of -5.6% and -7.9% relative strength vs SPY suggest fading momentum; a close below 220 would confirm further downside.
High ATR (3.93%) and -11.9% drawdown despite strong 26w return (+32.8%) suggest a volatile consolidation; waiting for RSI to reclaim 55 before acting.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Durable Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with expanding margins and accelerating earnings versus those suffering margin erosion despite top-line growth. S10 stands out with 62.5% YoY revenue growth, 56.0% net margin, and only $8.47B in total debt — the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 is similarly compelling at 34.2% net margin with 33.0% YoY net income growth on $14.79B of debt. On the other end, S02 posted a 61.2% YoY decline in net income despite 12.2% revenue growth, compressing net margin to just 2.1% on $80.14B of debt — a textbook case of paying for revenue without earnings power. S09 is the only name with negative revenue growth (-5.2% YoY) and declining net income (-12.3%), and I would need to see a top-line inflection before getting constructive.

views.note: 56% net margin, 62.5% revenue growth, minimal leverage at $8.47B debt — the strongest earnings profile in the universe by a wide margin.
34.2% net margin with 33% YoY net income growth and low debt of $14.79B supports durable earnings power.
35.7% net margin and 18.4% revenue growth are strong, though 12.5% net income growth lags revenue growth suggesting some margin pressure ahead.
$180B revenue with 38.2% net income growth is encouraging, but 11.8% net margin and $55.1B debt leave limited margin of safety if growth decelerates.
86.4% YoY net income growth is impressive but $90.68B in total debt is the second-highest in the universe; I need to see FCF and capex detail to get more constructive.
31% net margin is solid but $427.2B total debt dwarfs the group; earnings growth of 11.6% is modest relative to that leverage.
21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are respectable, but only 3% revenue growth limits upside conviction.
13% net margin with declining net income (-6.7% YoY) despite 9.5% revenue growth signals cost pressures; would turn constructive if margins stabilize.
Revenue declining 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3% and only 8.8% net margin — no earnings power to pay for here.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a razor-thin 2.1% margin on $80.14B of debt despite 12.2% revenue growth — classic cash-flow compression.

memos.headline: Fed in Mid-Cycle Easing With Sticky Inflation and Rising Unemployment — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Lean Away From Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has dropped 75bp over 12 months to 4.00%, with 50bp of that in the last three months alone, and the effective rate at 3.88% confirms follow-through. However, CPI is running +3.0% YoY with a +0.9% three-month gain, which is uncomfortably above target and limits the pace of further cuts. Unemployment at 4.40% — up 30bp over both three and twelve months — signals a softening labor market that justifies continued easing but also flags demand weakness for cyclicals. The 10y-2y spread has normalized sharply (+53bp YoY to +0.59pp), a classic early-easing steepening that benefits banks' net interest margins, while the 10y yield at 4.14% is essentially flat over three months, suggesting the long end is pricing in a cautious Fed. A CPI print above 3.3% YoY or unemployment breaking below 4.2% would challenge my easing-continues call and force a reassessment toward a pause regime.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits most from continued Fed easing and a stable long end at 4.14%.
Banks gain from the steepened curve (+59bp 10y-2y spread) improving net interest margins even as rate cuts compress short-end funding costs.
Staples offer defensive positioning given rising unemployment, but sticky 3% CPI erodes real margins — hold but don't add.
Cyclicals face headwinds from a softening labor market (unemployment +30bp to 4.4%) and uncertain consumer demand.
Energy is macro-ambiguous here — easing supports activity but rising unemployment signals demand risk; stay neutral until labor data clarifies.
Rate-sensitive sectors should benefit as the easing cycle continues and the 10y yield remains contained near 4.14%.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S07 and S03 Stand Out Positively While S04, S06, and S10 Flash Negative Signals
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. S07 posted an extraordinary +11.6% move on its 10/29 results, and S03 surged +9.6% on its 10/30 report—both suggesting strongly positive narrative shifts that may still have momentum given no subsequent negative filings. On the negative side, S04 dropped -2.9%, S06 fell -1.9%, and S10 declined -3.2% on their respective results disclosures, indicating the market received those narratives poorly. S08, S09, S01, and S02 all had muted reactions (ranging from -0.4% to +0.5%), suggesting sentiment is largely neutral and already priced. I have highest conviction on S07 and S03 where the positive tone shift was dramatic, and on S10 where the negative reaction was the most recent (11/19) and therefore least likely to be fully digested.

views.note: The +11.6% earnings-day reaction signals a powerful positive narrative shift that likely still has legs five weeks later.
A +9.6% earnings pop plus a benign follow-up 8-K on 11/20 suggest sustained positive sentiment momentum.
The -3.2% reaction on 11/19 results is the freshest negative signal in the universe and may not yet be fully priced.
A -2.9% earnings-day drop with no subsequent positive catalysts points to lingering negative sentiment.
Negative -1.9% earnings reaction followed by two additional filings without a clear positive catalyst keeps tone cautious.
A modest +2.5% earnings pop is constructive but not as decisive as S07 or S03; follow-up 8-K on 11/6 adds mild positive signal.
A flat +0.2% earnings reaction and high filing volume (six 8-Ks) suggest noise rather than a clear directional narrative.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and subsequent governance/personnel filings are sentiment-neutral.
A near-flat -0.4% earnings reaction with no follow-up filings leaves sentiment ambiguous.
Flat -0.3% earnings reaction plus management turnover and two Other Events filings create mixed but non-directional sentiment.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 82% m/m While Oil Slides—Geopolitical Risk Diverges from Credit Calm
memos.body: I am struck by the sharp divergence between the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 520.11 (+82% m/m, +34% 3m) and the relatively sanguine credit market with HY OAS at 2.88% (tightening 25bp m/m) and VIX at 15.78 (down 17% m/m). This tells me the market is pricing policy noise—likely around trade/tariff posturing and export controls—as transitory rather than structural, but I am not as comfortable dismissing it. WTI at $59.82 (-6.3% 3m) suggests either demand weakness or an easing of energy supply constraints, which could reflect geopolitical de-escalation on the energy front but also signals macro softness that could amplify any policy shock. Without granular detail in the 8-K filings beyond item codes, I have limited company-specific conviction, but the clustering of Reg FD and Other Events filings across S01, S09, and S06 in October-November hints at active investor communication during a period of elevated uncertainty. My base case is that the policy uncertainty spike is a structural shift—not a one-quarter event—and names with high China/export-control exposure or energy sensitivity warrant caution until we see concrete policy resolution.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in three weeks suggest active disclosure management amid policy uncertainty, but without content detail I cannot take a directional view.
Three filings in under three weeks including Reg FD and Other Events suggest the company is navigating a shifting policy landscape, but evidence is too thin for conviction.
Two 8-Ks in October (Reg FD + Other Events) during the early phase of the policy uncertainty ramp; I need clarity on whether disclosures relate to trade/sanctions exposure before taking a stance.
Single Reg FD filing in late October provides no actionable geopolitical signal; holding neutral pending further evidence.
With policy uncertainty at 520 and no 8-K filings to indicate proactive risk management, I worry about unhedged geopolitical exposure; would revisit if EPU drops below 400.
Single Other Events 8-K in early November is insufficient to assess geopolitical positioning amid the uncertainty spike.
